entries.description: A newspaper reports new defensive spells and charms, a complex array of counter-curses, and a small Auror task force specifically protecting Hogwarts.
entries.model_notes: Security state; the report withholds precise spell placement and perimeter geometry.

entries.description: Dumbledore identifies the Hogwarts kitchen as a workplace for the resident house-elves; Harry sends Kreacher to join them.
entries.model_notes: Functional and occupancy information only; this passage gives no kitchen position or dimensions.

entries.description: Buckbeak is staying with Hagrid, under the protective replacement name Witherwings. Hagrid subsequently reports that the Hippogriff is back in the open air.
entries.model_notes: Grounds creature state; no exact enclosure or position is specified here.

entries.description: Apparition is prohibited throughout Hogwarts buildings and grounds, a rule Harry states and Dumbledore confirms.
entries.model_notes: Apply to the whole grounds as well as the castle; exact boundary line is not supplied.

entries.description: Dumbledore describes a resident centaur herd in the Forest, recalling Umbridge’s encounter there.
entries.temporal: Summer 1996 account of previous school year
entries.model_notes: Establishes Forest inhabitants, without siting a settlement or clearing.

entries.description: Harry recalls that conversations with Dumbledore at Hogwarts usually take place across a desk.
entries.model_notes: Furniture and conversational arrangement; do not infer office dimensions from this recollection.

entries.description: Hermione says appointment as Quidditch captain gives Harry prefect-equivalent status, including use of the special prefects’ bathroom.
entries.model_notes: Access permission; no location, fittings or geometry are supplied here.

entries.description: The solid barrier between King’s Cross platforms nine and ten admits travellers to platform nine and three-quarters, where the scarlet, steam-emitting Hogwarts Express waits.
entries.model_notes: Off-site approach endpoint; retain the platform access relationship rather than treating King’s Cross as castle geometry. A historical memory also gives young Riddle a train ticket and instructs him to leave King’s Cross on 1 September; it supplies no additional platform geometry.

entries.description: Late in the journey the passing scenery is wild; Hogwarts becomes visible through the train window before the train slows and stops at a dark platform.
entries.model_notes: Visibility before arrival constrains an approach view. The half-hour estimate at P0187 is Harry’s judgement, not a measured travel time; no compass bearing is given.

entries.description: Compartments open from a corridor through sliding doors; door glazing can be screened with blinds. Luggage racks stand above seats, and swinging ceiling lanterns light the compartment brightly.
entries.model_notes: Ancillary transport interior if the arrival sequence is modelled; no exact dimensions. Distinguish corridor-facing glazing from exterior train windows.

entries.description: A lane leads from the station towards the school. Harry and Tonks walk uphill along the dark, deserted lane, following fresh carriage tracks; the walk feels substantially longer than Harry had appreciated from carriage travel.
entries.model_notes: Route and slope are explicit; perceived distance supplies no numerical length. The Thestral-carriage convoy at P0005 is imagined rather than witnessed in this scene.

entries.description: Lying in the train at the station, Harry thinks he can hear trees around the lake rustling and a distant owl.
entries.model_notes: Preserve the tentative auditory perception; it does not establish a station lakeshore view or exact distance to the lake.

entries.description: Tonks says she, Proudfoot, Savage and Dawlish are stationed in Hogsmeade to protect the school.
entries.model_notes: Security deployment in the village; no specific post, office or watchtower is identified.

entries.description: Tall pillars flank the gates, each pillar topped by a winged boar. On this late arrival the gates are chained and padlocked shut.
entries.model_notes: Model paired gateposts and their sculptures. Material and dimensions of the posts and gates are not specified in this passage.

entries.description: Alohomora does not release the padlock. Tonks says Dumbledore bewitched the gates and all perimeter walls carry anti-intruder jinxes. Snape opens the gates by tapping the padlock with his wand; the chains withdraw and the gates creak, then close with a clang and are resecured by another tap.
entries.model_notes: Observed gate behaviour supports an authorised-opening interaction. Tonks’s explanation of caster and wall jinxes is a report, not an observed attempted wall crossing; exact authorisation mechanism unspecified.

entries.description: From the gates a lantern can be seen at the distant foot of the castle. Snape approaches from there, then escorts Harry from the gates up to the castle steps.
entries.model_notes: Establish distance and line of sight between gates and castle foot without inventing bearings or a measured length.

entries.description: Castle steps lead to great oaken front doors opening into a vast flagstone-floored Entrance Hall. Open doors from the Entrance Hall transmit Great Hall talk, laughter and clinking crockery.
entries.model_notes: Direct front-door → Entrance Hall → Great Hall connection. Flagstone size, hall height and door dimensions unspecified.

entries.description: The Great Hall contains four long house tables with benches and a staff table at the top. Gryffindor’s table is furthest from the Entrance Hall; Harry passes the Hufflepuff table on his way there.
entries.model_notes: Relative ordering only: do not assign all four tables left-to-right or a compass direction from this walk alone.

entries.description: Floating candles illuminate the feast and make the plates glitter. Talk and laughter echo around the Hall.
entries.model_notes: Suspended magical lighting and reverberant acoustic character; no ceiling geometry added here.

entries.description: Chicken and chips vanish from the table and are replaced by puddings.
entries.model_notes: Temporary meal transition, not fixed table-top clutter; source mechanism not explained here.

entries.description: At this feast McGonagall sits beside Hagrid, Trelawney is on Hagrid’s other side, and Snape sits to Dumbledore’s right.
entries.model_notes: Dated seating arrangement, not permanent assigned chairs. P0078 also refers to Trelawney’s tower room without describing it.

entries.description: Dumbledore tells the assembled school that the castle’s magical fortifications were strengthened over the summer and reiterates restrictions including being out of bed after hours.
entries.model_notes: Broad security state, independent of the more specific gates and walls. Do not invent visible fortification additions.

entries.description: Hagrid reports that Dumbledore has arranged a new home for Grawp in a large cave up in the mountains, replacing his Forest home.
entries.model_notes: Mountain habitat beyond the Forest; no exact mountain, cave entrance, route or distance is supplied.

entries.description: Students climb through a portrait hole to leave the common room for the corridor; a queue forms at this opening.
entries.model_notes: An aperture requiring a climb, not merely a conventional full-height doorway; no size specified.

entries.description: The ceiling shows blue sky and thin wispy clouds matching the real sky visible through high mullioned windows.
entries.model_notes: Matching magical sky appearance and high subdivided windows; no statement of structural openness to weather.

entries.description: The common room contains a tapestry, which a flying Fanged Frisbee tries to bite, and is sunlit when Harry and Ron leave.
entries.model_notes: Tapestry subject and exact hanging position unspecified; daytime natural light reaches the room.

entries.description: The Defence Against the Dark Arts classroom is four floors below the Gryffindor common room, with a corridor outside its door.
entries.model_notes: Strong vertical relationship; count floors as narrated without assuming the building’s absolute floor numbering here.

entries.description: Drawn window curtains make the classroom gloomier than usual; candles light it. New wall pictures depict painful injuries and contorted bodies, including a shrieking witch, a blank-eyed wizard against a wall and a bloody mass on the ground.
entries.model_notes: Dated 1996–97 decoration and lighting state; pictured walls/bodies belong inside images, not the classroom geometry.

entries.description: Snape faces the seated class from behind his desk, walks around the room’s edge and back to the desk, then between practising students. Other desks occupy the classroom.
entries.model_notes: Teacher desk, student seating/desks and usable perimeter/interior circulation; no exact row arrangement specified.

entries.description: Harry identifies Acid Pops as the password for passing the gargoyle outside Dumbledore’s study.
entries.model_notes: Password current for this invitation; confirmation by actual entry is deferred to the next chapter.

entries.description: After the common-room study period the students follow a familiar path down to the dungeon classroom formerly taught in by Snape; a corridor lies outside its door.
entries.model_notes: Downward route and dungeon function; no exact stair sequence or total descent supplied.

entries.description: Three groups of four students occupy separate tables. An ingredient store cupboard supplies materials; a corner cupboard holds battered textbooks and tarnished scales. Slughorn has a desk at the front and can circulate between the tables.
entries.model_notes: Twelve-person class is an occupancy state, not total room capacity. It is not explicit whether the corner cupboard and ingredient store cupboard are the same fixture.

entries.description: Large bubbling cauldrons fill the dungeon with vapours and strong smells. A gold-coloured cauldron stands near Harry’s table, others near the Slytherin and Ravenclaw tables, and a small black cauldron sits on Slughorn’s desk. Later the room fills with bluish steam.
entries.model_notes: Lesson-specific vessels and effects. Amortentia’s perceived scent differs by observer, so Harry’s food/wood/flower notes are not a permanent ambient scent.

entries.location: Corridors between Gryffindor and headmaster entrance
entries.description: An unnamed statue along Harry’s route is large enough to hide him crouching behind it while Trelawney passes and pauses on its other side.
entries.model_notes: Local concealment and circulation constraint only; statue subject, material and exact corridor unspecified.

entries.description: A single gargoyle stands against the wall in a seventh-floor corridor. Saying Acid Pops makes it leap aside and the wall slide apart, revealing a moving spiral stone staircase that carries Harry upwards in smooth circles to the office door, which has a brass knocker.
entries.model_notes: Office access begins on seventh floor and rises. Do not place the office itself on the seventh-floor corridor level or assign an unmentioned higher floor number.

entries.description: The office is circular. Delicate silver instruments smoke and whirr on spindle-legged tables; portraits of former headmasters and headmistresses hang in frames; Fawkes has a perch behind the door.
entries.model_notes: Shape, furnishings, light motion/sound and perch-to-door relationship; exact count and portrait wall arrangement unspecified.

entries.description: A cabinet beside the door holds a shallow stone Pensieve with unusual markings around its rim. Dumbledore walks around his desk past Harry to retrieve it, then puts it on the desk in front of Harry.
entries.model_notes: Cabinet-door adjacency, desk and visitor seating relationship. Pensieve is movable; do not turn its lesson position into a permanent built-in basin.

entries.description: After a bottled silvery substance is poured into the Pensieve, Harry plunges his face into it and experiences falling into a memory scene. Dumbledore later takes his elbow and draws him out, returning them to their feet in the office.
entries.model_notes: Memory is a separate experiential space, not an actual geographical passage from the office to Little Hangleton.

entries.location: Headmaster office lamps and temporary display
entries.description: Extra lamps are lit by wand when the visitors return to the twilit office. A gold ring with a large cracked black stone stands on one of the small spindle-legged tables near Harry’s exit route.
entries.model_notes: Lamps are room fittings; ring is a dated display state rather than architecture. Exact table position relative to the door is not fixed by being noticed on departure.

entries.description: The sixth-years go outside to greenhouses for Herbology; dangerous plants include Venomous Tentacula capable of seizing a student unexpectedly from behind.
entries.model_notes: Exterior teaching structures and hazardous vegetation interaction; this passage supplies no greenhouse number or plan.

entries.description: Hagrid has a huge chair at the staff table; the Headmaster also has an identifiable chair there.
entries.model_notes: Differing chair scale/occupancy positions, without measured sizes or exact seating coordinates.

entries.description: Post owls swoop through the rain-flecked windows, scatter water droplets over diners and land at the tables.
entries.model_notes: Windows function as bird-entry openings. Rainy ceiling at P0013 is a sky appearance; Harry’s feeling of heat is embarrassment, not objective room temperature.

entries.description: From breakfast in the Great Hall the group goes down through cool misty drizzle to the Quidditch stadium, where Hermione takes a place in the stands.
entries.model_notes: Downward journey from castle to stadium; weather is a dated state, not permanent atmospheric specification.

entries.description: The stadium has a pitch with goalposts and groups of three goalhoops. Spectators sit in stands near the pitch edge, within view of applicants waiting there; Keeper trials take place airborne at the hoops.
entries.model_notes: Three hoops are explicit in Harry’s hyperbole about McLaggen’s width; that hyperbole supplies no usable width. No stadium capacity, hoop height or pitch dimensions given.

entries.description: After the trials the group leaves towards Hagrid’s cabin; later they hurry back through dark, deserted grounds to the castle and Great Hall entrance.
entries.model_notes: Grounds route connecting pitch, cabin and castle; no direct-distance or bearing claims. Weather clears to watery sunshine before dusk.

entries.description: The large grey Hippogriff Buckbeak is tethered in front of Hagrid’s cabin. Hagrid can come around the corner of the building with Fang behind him.
entries.model_notes: Directly observed tethering location supplements earlier reports. Animal approach involves reciprocal bows; no fence or enclosure is described.

entries.location: Hagrid cabin table and tea equipment
entries.description: Visitors sit around an enormous wooden table. Hagrid brews tea in an enormous copper kettle and serves bucket-sized mugs; the cabin has room to circulate around the table.
entries.model_notes: Relative giant-scale furnishings, material and circulation; avoid inventing exact scale ratios from metaphors.

entries.description: A large barrel in a corner contains slimy white writhing grubs roughly a foot long, making a squelching sound. People take the longer way round the table to avoid it.
entries.model_notes: Dated animal-food storage; the barrel’s relationship to a corner and circulation route is explicit.

entries.location: Aragog colony deep in Forbidden Forest
entries.description: Harry recalls that Aragog lives deep in the Forbidden Forest. Hagrid reports that the spider has been ill since summer and his family/colony is increasingly restless; he considers approaching unsafe for anyone except himself.
entries.model_notes: Habitat remembered by Harry and access danger reported by Hagrid. No new colony geometry or exact route; record ecological state without treating Hagrid’s safety judgement as a physical barrier.

entries.description: Hermione reports that Filch screened arriving students with Secrecy Sensors in the Entrance Hall and confiscated Crabbe’s shrunken head. She also relays Filch’s statement that incoming owls are checked.
entries.model_notes: Operational 1996 security state; Harry himself missed screening due to late arrival, so it is not a universal impenetrable check.

entries.location: Gryffindor common room and dormitory access
entries.description: The crowded common room has tables and chairs; a door leads towards the boys’ dormitories.
entries.model_notes: Door connection and study furniture. This passage does not specify stairs beyond that door.

entries.description: Storm-driven wind and sleet strike the dormitory windows. Harry reads in bed; Ron can be magically suspended above his own mattress and fall back onto it. Neville, Dean and Seamus are also present when the room wakes.
entries.model_notes: Shared sleeping room with windows and headroom above a bed. The suspension supplies no reliable ceiling height.

entries.description: Filch stands at the oak front doors checking the names of students permitted to visit Hogsmeade and triple-checking them with a long, thin Secrecy Sensor. On return he approaches across the Entrance Hall with the Sensor, but McGonagall exempts her group.
entries.model_notes: Observed screening in both travel directions; portable equipment and staff procedure, not a permanent gate or detector installation.

entries.description: The road out of the school grounds leads to Hogsmeade. The return goes up the village High Street and uphill along a lane to Hogwarts. The lane bends, has a hedgerow, and eventually enters the grounds before reaching the castle stone steps.
entries.model_notes: Winding uphill return with hedged edge; no precise road length, bearings or identification of every gate crossing in this scene.

entries.description: Strong wind and thick sleet accompany the village trip; frozen slush covers the return road. The landscape by the lane appears deserted while the wind roars.
entries.model_notes: Dated seasonal surface, weather and sound state; do not make permanent snow cover.

entries.description: Zonko’s is boarded up on this visit, while Honeydukes is open and crowded. The Three Broomsticks is reached after leaving Honeydukes and walking along the village street; departure from the pub leads back up the High Street towards Hogwarts.
entries.model_notes: Boundary-excursion waypoints and temporary shop closure; no exact inter-building distances or full village street plan.

entries.description: The pub has tables, a bar, and an interior pillar near Harry’s table. Leanne says Katie returned from its bathroom carrying a parcel; the text explicitly leaves open whether she received it inside the bathroom.
entries.model_notes: Limited village interior context tied to the attempted castle delivery; no bathroom floor level or adjacency is established. Katie later remembers pushing the ladies’ door open, but a person behind it is her deduction, not a recovered observation.

entries.description: McGonagall meets the group on the castle’s stone steps, takes them through the Entrance Hall and upstairs to her office. Afterward the students climb further stairs to the Gryffindor common room.
entries.model_notes: Office lies above Entrance Hall and below at least some of the route to Gryffindor; exact floor not stated.

entries.description: Sleet hits the windows, which rattle in their frames. The office remains chilly despite a fire in a grate. McGonagall closes the door and moves around her desk to face the visitors.
entries.model_notes: Windows, fireplace, desk and door, plus storm-specific temperature/sound. Desk position gives no complete room plan.

entries.description: McGonagall sends Leanne up to the hospital wing and later says she will go up there herself.
entries.model_notes: Upward route described from this office; do not infer an absolute hospital floor number.

entries.location: Gryffindor portrait entrance and common-room fire
entries.description: Hermione gives the Fat Lady the password Dilligrout and the portrait swings open into the common room. The crowded room smells of damp clothing after students return from the storm; desirable armchairs stand by the fire.
entries.model_notes: Observed password access, swinging portrait, fireplace seating and a dated wet-clothing state; distinguish this entrance from a generic door.

entries.location: Headmaster office Pensieve lighting and display
entries.description: The Pensieve stands on the desk and throws silver flecks of light over the ceiling. Dumbledore can raise a small revolving three-dimensional-looking memory figure above its swirling contents, then shake it back down.
entries.model_notes: Magical visual state, distinct from fully entering a memory; figure is memory projection rather than an actual room occupant.

entries.description: Phineas Nigellus Black occupies one of the portraits on the office wall, can speak and rise from an apparent sleeping pose, and walks out of his frame.
entries.model_notes: Narration supposes he is visiting his other portrait at Grimmauld Place; that destination is not visually followed here. Record frame exit as observed and destination as inferred by narration.

entries.location: Headmaster office windows and cleared table
entries.description: The office has windows through which Dumbledore indicates the dark sky. Marvolo’s ring, displayed on a little table at the previous lesson, is no longer there.
entries.model_notes: Dated removal of a loose display object; the table remains. Window size, count and bearing unspecified.

entries.description: The route to Herbology crosses a vegetable patch before the greenhouses. Returning mist makes finding the correct greenhouse slower than usual.
entries.model_notes: Grounds waypoint and limited visibility; greenhouse count, numbering and patch position relative to castle unspecified.

entries.description: Students work in groups around gnarled Snargaluff stumps. A stump sends long thorny bramble-like vines out of its top; a central opening contracts around an inserted arm. Removing a pulsating green grapefruit-sized pod makes the vines retract, leaving a dead-looking stump.
entries.model_notes: Term-specific plant installation and animation states. Do not model the apparently dead stump without its active volume.

entries.description: The greenhouse has glass sides against which a thrown pod rebounds. Work equipment includes protective gloves/goggles, gum shields, secateurs, bowls and a trowel used to process pods.
entries.model_notes: Glass envelope and movable class equipment, not a precise greenhouse plan or proof of workbench geometry.

entries.description: After Transfiguration, several conjured yellow birds continue flying and twittering around the classroom, with droppings falling from above.
entries.model_notes: Lesson aftermath and animated state; no fixed bird population.

entries.description: The team uses a changing room before and after playing; it has a door and a place for Harry to hang up his robes.
entries.model_notes: Support room connected with pitch activity; no locker, bench, shower or exact entrance placement is specified.

entries.description: Returning from Quidditch to the castle, Harry and Ron reach the second floor and push aside a tapestry to use their usual shortcut up to Gryffindor Tower. Behind it is a corridor. They later hurry up stairs and along a seventh-floor corridor to the Fat Lady, then climb into the common room.
entries.model_notes: Connect second-floor tapestry to a route ending at seventh-floor portrait entrance. The shortcut’s internal stair/floor sequence is not completely narrated; P0086 is Harry’s fantasy and adds no geometry.

entries.description: Harry lies in a four-poster bed with a canopy overhead and a pillow he can rearrange.
entries.model_notes: Bed type and canopy, without fabric colour or dimensions in this passage.

entries.location: First match frost and house colours
entries.description: Frosty grass crunches on the walk down to the stadium and the pitch ground is frozen. One stadium end is filled with red-and-gold supporters and the other with green-and-silver supporters under a clear blue sky.
entries.model_notes: Seasonal surface and crowd arrangement; colours are supporters’ display, not proof of permanent stand decoration.

entries.description: The commentator stands on a podium and speaks through a magical megaphone. Harry can look towards it from his broom over the playing area.
entries.model_notes: Location within viewing range of flight/pitch; no height or exact side specified. P0149’s “grounds” should not be expanded into an unsupported entire-school flyover.

entries.description: Ginny crashes into the commentator’s podium, reducing it to wooden wreckage with Zacharias beneath it; the team lands beside the wreckage.
entries.temporal: End of first Gryffindor–Slytherin match, autumn 1996
entries.model_notes: Establishes wood construction and dated destruction. No subsequent repair is yet described.

entries.description: A crowded common-room celebration includes a drinks table and Butterbeer. People in a corner are in full view of the room.
entries.model_notes: Temporary party furnishing and visibility within room, not a complete room-wide isovist or permanent bar.

entries.description: After leaving the Fat Lady’s portrait into a deserted corridor, Harry finds Hermione in the first unlocked classroom he tries. It has a teacher’s desk and a swinging door; a small conjured flock circles her head and later attacks Ron.
entries.model_notes: An accessible unnamed classroom along Harry’s search route. “First unlocked” does not establish that it is the first door or immediately adjacent to the portrait; floor number not explicitly repeated.

entries.description: Snow swirls against icy windows. The Great Hall receives twelve Christmas trees; stair banisters are wound with holly and tinsel; everlasting candles glow inside armour helmets; large mistletoe bunches hang at intervals in corridors.
entries.model_notes: Dated decoration across several spaces; armour positions, stair identities and tree distribution within Hall unspecified.

entries.description: Harry uses his knowledge of secret passageways to navigate between classes while avoiding mistletoe-blocked corridors.
entries.model_notes: Multiple alternate interior routes exist, but none is named or mapped in this passage.

entries.description: Harry and Hermione work at a table with bookshelves behind them. The shelves are dark enough for someone nearby to remain unseen until Madam Pince comes around a corner carrying a lamp. Conversations are whispered and the library closes at night.
entries.model_notes: Shelf/table relationship, local concealment, portable lighting and use constraints. No shelf rows, room outline or full lighting plan established.

entries.description: Hermione explains that Secrecy Sensors detect jinxes, curses and concealment charms, but a love potion merely repackaged as perfume or cough medicine escapes that check unless Filch recognises it.
entries.model_notes: Important limit on 1996 entry screening. Hermione’s judgement of love-potion danger is not adopted as a modelling fact; no barrier should be treated as perfectly all-detecting.

entries.description: After library closing Harry and Hermione return along deserted lamp-lit corridors to the Fat Lady. The current festive password is Baubles; the portrait swings forwards and they climb through its hole.
entries.model_notes: Artificial corridor lighting and dated access credential; no exact floors or stair sequence in this route.

entries.description: Students practise human transfiguration in front of mirrors. Harry later finds Hermione emerging from a girls’ bathroom on the floor below the Transfiguration classroom.
entries.model_notes: Mirrors as teaching equipment and a one-floor vertical relationship. Do not identify this bathroom as Myrtle’s merely because Luna initially mistakes crying for Myrtle at P0061.

entries.description: Along the corridor walked after the girls’ bathroom encounter, a chandelier hangs overhead; Peeves dangles upside-down from it as Harry and Luna pass underneath.
entries.model_notes: Ceiling light fixture and overhead clearance in an unnamed corridor. Exact floor/corridor not stated.

entries.description: Harry meets Luna in the Entrance Hall, then leads her up the marble staircase to Slughorn’s office. Party music, laughter and conversation become louder as they approach.
entries.model_notes: Upward route from Entrance Hall; no total floors traversed or claim that office directly opens onto the staircase.

entries.location: Slughorn office party volume and hangings
entries.description: Slughorn’s office is much larger than an ordinary teacher’s study, though Harry cannot tell whether this is built space or magical enlargement. Emerald, crimson and gold hangings drape the walls and ceiling, making a tent-like interior.
entries.model_notes: Preserve uncertainty about the room’s underlying size and magical expansion; fabric conceals the architectural surfaces.

entries.location: Slughorn office party lighting and service
entries.description: An ornate golden lamp hangs from the ceiling centre, filled with fluttering luminous fairies and bathing the crowded stuffy room in red light. Singing with mandolin-like accompaniment comes from a distant corner; pipe smoke hazes part of the room. House-elves carry heavy silver food platters through the crowd; mistletoe is present.
entries.model_notes: Event-specific lighting, atmosphere, food service and decorations; no permanent dining tables are established by the elves’ table-like appearance.

entries.location: Last classroom in Slughorn office corridor
entries.description: Harry leaves the party into a deserted corridor, listens at successive doors, and hears Snape and Draco through the keyhole of the last classroom. Party noise masks Harry’s footsteps. Draco exits that classroom, passes Slughorn’s open office door and rounds a distant corner; Snape returns to the party.
entries.model_notes: Classroom on the same corridor, with a sound-transmitting keyhole and a further corner. No room fittings described; do not invent a direct classroom-office door.

entries.description: While trying to find Snape, Harry considers his office in the dungeons as a possible destination.
entries.model_notes: Narration supplies the office’s dungeon location as background; the proposed journey there does not occur, so it establishes no travelled connection from the party.

entries.location: Temporary Floo arrival at McGonagall office
entries.description: A Ministry-arranged one-off Floo Network connection returns pupils to Hogwarts after New Year. Saying Hogwarts in the Burrow kitchen fire brings Harry into McGonagall’s office fireplace; he climbs over its grate, and she warns him about ash on the carpet.
entries.model_notes: Temporary network permission, destination fireplace, grate and carpet. Do not assume unrestricted public Floo access in other periods.

entries.description: On leaving McGonagall’s office towards Gryffindor Tower, Harry looks through corridor windows over deeply snow-covered grounds. In the distance he sees Hagrid feeding Buckbeak in front of the cabin as the sun sinks.
entries.model_notes: Line of sight from an unspecified corridor on this route to cabin frontage; window and sun compass bearings unspecified.

entries.description: The Fat Lady rejects Baubles because the password has changed, then accepts Abstinence and swings forwards to reveal the portrait hole.
entries.model_notes: Dated access state; refusal concerns obsolete password, not a physical malfunction.

entries.location: Portrait of drunken monks by Charms corridor
entries.description: Hermione reports that the Fat Lady and Violet drank wine inside a picture of drunken monks down by the Charms corridor.
entries.model_notes: Portrait subject and approximate corridor relationship; wine and apparent intoxication are portrait-world behaviour, not physical wine on the corridor floor.

entries.description: Common-room noticeboards carry a newly pinned Apparition-lesson sign, beneath which eligible students can sign their names.
entries.model_notes: Fixed communication fixture and dated paper notice; no board count or exact mounting position.

entries.description: During a water-conjuring lesson, Seamus produces a hose-like jet that strikes the classroom ceiling and rebounds onto Flitwick.
entries.model_notes: Dated demonstration effect confirms an overhead surface; supplies no ceiling height or permanent water feature.

entries.location: Headmaster office January light, sounds and rug
entries.description: Lamps provide soft golden light; former-headmaster portraits snore in their frames and Fawkes makes low musical cries behind Harry. A rug lies in front of the desk where returning Pensieve visitors land.
entries.model_notes: Repeated furnishing evidence with rug-to-desk relationship and phoenix sound; no new frame positions.

entries.description: The ancient Sorting Hat sits unmoving on a shelf above Dumbledore’s head.
entries.model_notes: Shelf position relative to seated Headmaster; do not infer a specific wall or shelf height.

entries.location: Trophy room shields and school records
entries.description: Dumbledore reports that Riddle searched shields in the trophy room and prefect lists in old school records for evidence of his father.
entries.model_notes: Trophy-room shield display and existence of old records; storage site of those records is not specified.

entries.description: In the recollection, Slughorn sits in a comfortable winged armchair with his feet on a velvet pouffe, holding wine and crystallised pineapple. Half a dozen teenage boys sit around him on harder or lower seats. A small golden clock on the desk chimes eleven; Slughorn carries his glass to the desk as the boys leave.
entries.temporal: Riddle’s teenage school years, memory viewed January 1997
entries.model_notes: The first view in chapter 17 is tampered with; the later genuine memory repeats and supports these furnishings. White fog in the earlier version is a memory-edit artefact, not physical office atmosphere. The clock stands on the desk behind Slughorn’s chair.

entries.description: Harry and Hermione stand in a deserted courtyard during break; the snow is ankle-deep.
entries.model_notes: Unnamed courtyard and relative snow depth; no plan, paving or enclosure described.

entries.location: Potions work stations and store contents
entries.description: Students use stools at shared worktables with cauldrons heated by individual fires. Slughorn’s desk is at the front of the dungeon. The store cupboard contains unicorn horns, tangles of dried herbs and, at the back, a card box of brown shrivelled bezoars.
entries.model_notes: Additional storage contents and heating method. Shared table is also called a desk; do not create an extra fixture from wording variation.

entries.description: Hermione reports searching the library’s restricted section for Horcrux explanations. An old borrowed book, Magick Moste Evile, gives a ghostly wail when slammed shut.
entries.model_notes: Book behaviour directly observed; completeness of her search is reported. No restricted-section entrance or shelving geometry is described here.

entries.description: Snow melts as February arrives, giving way to cold persistent rain beneath low purple-grey clouds. The lawns become slippery and muddy; late February adds wind.
entries.model_notes: Dated terrain surface and weather, replacing January snow state.

entries.description: The Hall’s tables disappear for the lesson, leaving floor space for pupils. Rain strikes the high windows and the enchanted ceiling swirls darkly above. Students are instructed to leave five feet clear in front of each person, and wooden hoops appear on the dusty floor at their destinations.
entries.model_notes: Temporary teaching layout with explicit five-foot displacement exemplified by Susan’s Splinching. No hoop diameter or Hall dimension supplied; tables are absent, not destroyed.

entries.description: Twycross explains that Dumbledore has lifted Hogwarts’s anti-Apparition enchantment only inside the Great Hall and only for one hour. He warns that nobody can Apparate beyond the Hall’s walls. Students attempt local moves; Twycross vanishes and reappears at the back of the Hall. The hoops vanish after the lesson.
entries.model_notes: Rule and duration are reported; local Apparition is witnessed. Maintain a bounded temporary exception, not unrestricted Apparition on the grounds.

entries.description: Returning to Gryffindor Tower, Harry and Ron meet a fourth-floor door jammed shut by Peeves. They turn back and use a familiar shortcut, reaching the portrait hole within five minutes.
entries.model_notes: Local blocked-door event and alternate route; time is narrative travel time at a run, not a scale ruler or complete shortcut map.

entries.description: A door off the common room leads to the boys’ staircase and up to the dormitory, which contains pupils’ beds and trunks. Ron’s bed has a post, and the dormitory has a rain-washed window.
entries.model_notes: Explicit door → stair → dormitory relationship. No spiral form or exact number of beds added by this passage.

entries.location: Marauder’s Map depiction and missing locations
entries.description: The activated Map depicts detailed plans of castle floors and labelled moving dots for occupants. It shows a Slytherin common room and dormitory, Snape’s study, bathrooms and hospital wing; Draco periodically cannot be found despite Crabbe and Goyle appearing in corridors.
entries.model_notes: Diegetic map evidence, not supplied coordinates. Apparent completeness at P0121 is limited by observed disappearances; do not invent missing-room geometry or assume Draco has left the grounds.

entries.description: Notices on every common-room noticeboard announce cancellation of the next Hogsmeade visit.
entries.model_notes: Temporary access restriction, not physical closure of the road or village.

entries.description: Slughorn’s study is overheated and crowded. Ron trips over a tasselled footstool, then sits in an armchair. A table is loaded with drinks; another low table lies across Harry’s route to Slughorn’s open potion kit, which Harry jumps to reach.
entries.model_notes: Footstool, armchair, drinks table, low table and kit locations constrain local circulation but do not establish the whole floor plan. Kit is movable and antidote supplies are a dated state.

entries.description: The ward has double doors, curtained windows and lamps. Beds have bedside cabinets and visitors can pull chairs around a bed. Ron is initially the only patient; visitors wait outside and try to see in as doors open.
entries.model_notes: Ward entrance, furnishings and sight restriction. Six-visitors rule is staff policy, not physical capacity. Narration calls these ward doors “dormitory doors”.

entries.description: Harry recounts that McGonagall and Pomfrey brought the poisoned Ron up from Slughorn’s room to the hospital wing.
entries.model_notes: Reported upward transfer, no absolute floor numbers or full stair path.

entries.description: Leaving the ward, Harry, Hermione and Hagrid walk along a corridor towards the marble staircase. Further along the return route a corner lets Filch’s shadow appear on the wall before he turns into view; a turning leads towards Gryffindor Tower.
entries.model_notes: Route sequence only; does not prove each described segment is adjacent or fix staircase landing level.

entries.location: Disguised wall door shortcut to Potions
entries.description: Harry escapes a conversation by stepping sideways through a door masquerading as solid wall and running along a shortcut towards Potions.
entries.model_notes: Concealed interior doorway and route destination; exact position and mechanism not described.

entries.description: At the Hufflepuff match there is little wind, broken cloud and intermittent dazzling sunlight. Luna and McGonagall occupy a commentator’s podium below Harry’s aerial viewpoint, using the magical megaphone.
entries.model_notes: A podium is functioning again after the earlier collision; text does not say whether repaired or replaced. Do not infer repair method. Match sound carries over the grounds.

entries.location: Hospital bed light and exterior sky
entries.description: Harry wakes in a warm comfortable hospital bed with Ron on his left; a lamp casts a golden circle onto the shadowed ceiling and crimson-streaked indigo sky is visible outside.
entries.model_notes: Local bed adjacency and light effect. Ron’s statement that he heard the match commentary from the ward (P0166) supplies an additional reported acoustic connection.

entries.location: Hospital nighttime controls and Pomfrey office
entries.description: Pomfrey’s office opens into the ward. At bedtime she waves her wand to close all curtains, the lamps dim, and she returns through her office door. Harry later casts Muffliato towards that door and no response follows the noisy disturbance in the ward.
entries.model_notes: Curtain referents may include bed screens or windows; the passage says all curtains, so do not arbitrarily choose. Spell does not prove a naturally soundproof office.

entries.description: Calling Kreacher’s name produces a loud crack followed by Kreacher and Dobby wrestling on the ward floor. Peeves appears in midair above them and swoops around a lamp.
entries.model_notes: Observed instantaneous elf arrival inside the castle despite human Apparition restrictions. This scene does not explicitly name the travel mechanism or show their origin.

entries.description: On the route from hospital discharge down to breakfast the group turns into a seventh-floor corridor with a tapestry depicting trolls in tutus. Continuing towards the Great Hall brings them to the foot of the marble staircase.
entries.model_notes: Route passes seventh floor, but the hospital’s own floor is not explicitly numbered here. Tapestry is a fixed landmark; the girl’s scales are carried, not room furnishings.

entries.location: Headmaster entrance new password and clock
entries.description: Toffee eclairs makes the gargoyle leap aside. Harry climbs the spiral staircase two steps at a time and hears a clock inside the office chime eight. The door is opened from inside; Trelawney descends the same staircase.
entries.model_notes: Dated credential and walkable moving-stair route; no measured riser count. Pensieve and memory bottles remain movable desk equipment.

entries.description: Armando Dippet’s portrait hangs above Dumbledore’s head and makes little grunting snores.
entries.model_notes: Named portrait and position above Headmaster, without exact dimensions or wall coordinates.

entries.description: Dumbledore describes Hogwarts as a stronghold of ancient magic, suggesting that Voldemort may have wished to uncover further secrets and stores of magic there.
entries.model_notes: Dumbledore’s interpretation of Voldemort’s aims remains speculation; the passage provides no new hidden-room location or visible magical installation.

entries.location: Headmaster office in Voldemort application memory
entries.description: The remembered office has Fawkes on his perch, Dumbledore’s desk and a visitor’s seat apparently the same as Harry’s current chair. Snow falls past a window and builds on its outside ledge. The cabinet now used for the Pensieve then holds bottles, from which Dumbledore serves wine.
entries.temporal: Undated snowy evening after Dumbledore becomes Headmaster, recalled March 1997
entries.model_notes: Historical layout continuity with changed cabinet contents and weather. “Same seat” is Harry’s visual judgement, not confirmed furniture provenance; no invented calendar year.

entries.description: Dumbledore says that since refusing Voldemort the Defence teaching post, no subsequent teacher has lasted longer than a year.
entries.model_notes: Reported magical constraint on the post; do not locate a curse source in the classroom or invent a visible fixture.

entries.description: Kreacher reports that Draco sleeps in a dormitory in the dungeons.
entries.model_notes: Explicit reported vertical zone, not a measured depth or fully mapped entrance.

entries.location: Room of Requirement concealed seventh-floor entrance
entries.description: The Room’s concealed entrance lies in a stretch of wall on the seventh floor opposite the tapestry of Barnabas the Barmy teaching ballet to trolls. An approach corner and corridor allow lookouts to wait outside.
entries.model_notes: Tapestry identifies the earlier tutu-troll landmark. Door location is precise relative to tapestry, not to a compass direction; no visible doorway when unavailable.

entries.description: Harry walks past three times concentrating on several requests to see what Draco is doing; no door appears. The exposed stone is solid under a push and later a kick, and repeated attempts over an hour and on another visit fail.
entries.model_notes: Observed request-dependent denial. Dobby says entry is impossible, while Hermione proposes that knowing the exact required room is necessary; those interpretations are not a universal proven access algorithm.

entries.location: Room of Requirement mapping and requirement theory
entries.description: Harry says he has never seen the Room on the Marauder’s Map. Hermione suggests it can be unplottable when required, and that Draco entered the DA headquarters by knowing precisely what room to request, whereas Harry does not know Draco’s room.
entries.model_notes: Preserve hypotheses as hypotheses; map omission is corroborated on the later visit at P0151. Do not make user speculation into a fixed geometry rule.

entries.location: Headmaster entrance relative to Room corridor
entries.description: Harry tells Tonks that Dumbledore’s office is around the other side of the castle from this Room of Requirement corridor, behind the gargoyle.
entries.model_notes: Both entrances have seventh-floor evidence, but are geographically separated around the castle; no exact distance or bearing.

entries.description: Inspecting the Map, Harry sees Gryffindors in one tower, Ravenclaws in another, Slytherins in the dungeons and Hufflepuffs in a basement near the kitchens.
entries.model_notes: Narrated interpretation of a diegetic map; preserve distinct towers and basement/dungeon zones without supplying unshown coordinates or treating “near” as a shared wall.

entries.description: An old tiled boys’ bathroom contains a cracked mirror and toilets in cubicles behind the boys. Myrtle rises from one toilet, floats in midair, is visible in the mirror, and dives back in, splashing water onto the floor; voices echo.
entries.model_notes: Fixture relationships and acoustics; no floor identified in this scene. Myrtle says she lives in a different girls’ bathroom but can visit other places, so this is not her usual bathroom.

entries.description: On an unanswered office visit Harry is sure he hears a quickly stifled old gramophone.
entries.model_notes: Unconfirmed auditory identification; do not present the exact device or its position as visually inspected.

entries.description: A notice offers extra supervised Apparition practice in Hogsmeade. Students queue at Filch’s Entrance Hall screening before leaving. Ron later reports aiming for outside Madam Puddifoot’s and arriving near Scrivenshaft’s; the group visits the Three Broomsticks afterward.
entries.model_notes: School-to-village permitted training and destinations; no exact spacing inferred from Ron’s overshoot. Distinguish practice permission from the cancelled recreational visit.

entries.location: House-elf Disapparition in Gryffindor common room
entries.description: Kreacher and Dobby appear with cracks by the common-room fire, then Kreacher explicitly Disapparates and Dobby vanishes after giving their reports.
entries.model_notes: Confirms elf Disapparition inside castle independently of human anti-Apparition rules. Arrival position is near the group/fire, not an invented fixed teleport point.

entries.description: Blue sky appears over castle turrets. The courtyard has a sunny corner where pupils sit; a bell sounds overhead in the castle and pupils head from there towards the Entrance Hall.
entries.model_notes: Turreted silhouette, courtyard corner and audible school bell; do not infer an explicitly visible bell tower.

entries.description: While waiting in the common room, the group judges the time as the sun sinks to the Forbidden Forest treetops, then goes up to the boys’ dormitory; Harry returns down the stairs and through the open doorway into the common room.
entries.model_notes: Narrative sunset sight context from the common-room scene; no window position is specified, so bearing remains unresolved.

entries.description: Harry reaches the Entrance Hall and finds the front door unlocked, opens it, smells fresh air and grass, and walks down the front steps into dusk.
entries.model_notes: A lapse in the intended evening lock, not permanent unrestricted exit. Slughorn confirms concern about security.

entries.description: At the bottom of the castle steps Harry chooses to go past the vegetable patch, which is not strictly on the route to Hagrid’s. He hides behind a low stone wall there. Sprout later walks towards her greenhouses, while Slughorn can look towards the black Forest and distant cabin lights.
entries.model_notes: Patch is a detour, with a low stone concealment wall and views towards Forest/cabin; no exact plot boundary or compass orientation supplied.

entries.location: Forest spider colony after Aragog’s death
entries.description: Hagrid reports that after Aragog dies the other spiders no longer let him near their webs and would eat him; extracting the body is difficult because the colony normally eats its dead.
entries.model_notes: Changed access danger and web habitat; no magical barrier or precise colony location added.

entries.location: Hagrid rear window and back garden
entries.description: A rear window of the hut looks onto the garden behind it, where Aragog’s enormous body lies on its back with legs curled. The burial site is beyond the pumpkin patch.
entries.model_notes: Front/rear distinction, window view and patch-to-grave relationship. No extra rear door is explicitly described despite the group stepping out into the back garden.

entries.description: A massive pit in the back garden lies beside a ten-foot-high heap of excavated earth. Moonlight through trees mingles with light from the hut window to illuminate the body at the pit edge. Hagrid rolls Aragog in; Slughorn levitates the earth over it, leaving a smooth mound.
entries.model_notes: Ten feet describes spoil-heap height, not grave depth. Record the filled grave as the resulting terrain feature and the open pit as the funeral state.

entries.description: A compost heap stands near enough to the open grave for Hagrid to collapse onto it during the funeral.
entries.model_notes: Garden feature adjacent to burial activity without precise spacing.

entries.location: Hagrid cabin dog basket and candle
entries.description: Fang has a basket inside the cabin. People sit at the table with bucket-sized mugs; a candle between Harry and Slughorn flickers in Hagrid’s snores and later gutters.
entries.model_notes: Additional dog furniture, table arrangement and candle lighting; wine bottles are movable funeral gathering supplies.

entries.description: Several brass pots and a long silky skein of bright white unicorn hair hang from the ceiling. Hagrid says Forest branches catch the hair from unicorn tails and he uses it to bind bandages; later he gives the whole tail to Slughorn.
entries.model_notes: Observed overhead storage with material/colour; unicorn occurrence and collection method are reported. Hair is removed during this scene, so do not retain it as a permanent post-funeral fixture.

entries.location: Hagrid’s school cupboard for young Aragog
entries.description: Hagrid recalls keeping Aragog in a cupboard up at the school when the spider was young.
entries.model_notes: Historical animal-hiding cupboard only; exact room, floor, size and survival are unspecified.

entries.description: The front door remains unlocked on Harry’s return after the burial. On the third floor he dodges Peeves through a sideways shortcut, then climbs higher to the Fat Lady’s portrait and the hard corridor floor outside it.
entries.model_notes: Third-floor shortcut on upward route; no complete internal shortcut shape or exact travel time.

entries.description: The Fat Lady initially refuses entry claiming a midnight password change, then admits she lied because Harry woke her. The password is still Tapeworm.
entries.model_notes: Do not implement a midnight reset from the retracted claim; this scene demonstrates discretionary refusal by the portrait occupant.

entries.description: Nearly Headless Nick says the Bloody Baron is groaning and clanking up on the Astronomy Tower, a favourite activity.
entries.model_notes: Tower occupancy/sound report, without layout or certainty that sounds are heard at the portrait corridor.

entries.description: Every portrait around the office walls is awake and listening; one depicts a fat red-nosed wizard who uses an ear trumpet.
entries.model_notes: Additional portrait subject/prop and animated reaction, not a real ear trumpet lying in the room.

entries.description: A ruby-encrusted sword rests in a glass case on the wall behind Dumbledore; he identifies it as the surviving known Gryffindor relic.
entries.model_notes: Observed wall position, glass enclosure and jewelled sword. Provenance is Dumbledore’s statement; no case dimensions supplied.

entries.description: Ron’s misdirected wand makes large fake snowflakes fall from the classroom ceiling onto nearby pupils. They work at neighbouring tables with glass flasks; Flitwick shelters under a table when a flask explodes.
entries.model_notes: Lesson-specific spell effect and work furniture; not weather penetrating the castle.

entries.description: The common room is sunny and contains a table at a window where the trio sit to talk.
entries.model_notes: Table-window relationship; no bearing or proof this is the same table used on previous occasions.

entries.description: From a seventh-floor detour Harry sees Draco’s Map dot in a boys’ bathroom one floor below. After colliding with a suit of armour, he runs down a marble staircase and along the lower passage to the bathroom door; he later returns there from the Room’s seventh-floor corridor.
entries.model_notes: Bathroom is on the floor below seventh, thus sixth in this numbering. The text calls this staircase marble; retain that statement without silently equating it with the Entrance Hall’s principal marble staircase.

entries.location: Boys’ bathroom sink, mirror and fixtures
entries.description: A grimy sink basin faces a cracked mirror in which Draco sees Harry standing behind him near the door. The tiled bathroom has toilet cubicles, a wall lamp beside Harry and a bin behind him; a cistern is beneath Myrtle’s hovering position.
entries.model_notes: Fixture/view relationships and reverberation. Repeated cracked mirror and Myrtle connect this scene with chapter 21’s bathroom; no exact room dimensions.

entries.location: Boys’ bathroom duel damage and flooding
entries.description: A missed hex shatters the wall lamp, another blast explodes the bin, and a rebounding spell smashes a toilet cistern. Water floods the tiled floor, makes it slippery and mixes with Draco’s blood. The room remains wrecked and soaked when Snape questions Harry.
entries.model_notes: Dated damaged fixture and floor state; no subsequent repair is narrated here. Injury-related visual shimmer at P0090 is not structural transformation.

entries.location: Room of Requirement hiding request and door
entries.description: Harry walks three times before the blank seventh-floor wall asking for a place to hide his book; a door appears and he enters. On leaving he slams the door and it immediately turns back into stone.
entries.model_notes: Successful hiding-room state despite earlier failed requests about Draco. Door concealment is observed; do not infer that all possible users obtain separate inventories.

entries.location: Room of hidden objects volume and light
entries.description: The room is the size of a large cathedral. High windows send shafts of light over a city-like mass of stored objects, with many alleys and road-like passages between towering piles of damaged furniture and hidden goods.
entries.model_notes: Narrated scale analogy and navigable maze of objects, not a literal town or calibrated dimensions. Claimed generations of use and reasons for hiding items are Harry’s interpretation.

entries.description: The piles contain thousands of books, winged catapults and Fanged Frisbees still hovering weakly, chipped bottles of congealed potions, hats, jewels, cloaks, apparent dragon eggshells, corked bottles with sinister shimmering contents, rusty swords and a heavy bloodstained axe.
entries.model_notes: Inventory groups and materials/condition for storage ambience. Eggshell identification is tentative; no need to copy thousands of individual carried-object instances.

entries.description: Entering an alley, Harry turns right past an enormous stuffed troll, continues briefly, then turns left at the broken Vanishing Cabinet in which Montague had been lost. He reaches a large cupboard with a blistered, apparently acid-damaged surface.
entries.model_notes: Exact local turn sequence and landmarks; no corridor lengths or absolute bearings. Acid is Harry’s explanation of visible blistering, not confirmed chemical cause.

entries.description: The cupboard has creaking doors and contains a cage holding a long-dead five-legged skeleton. Harry hides his book behind the cage, then moves a chipped bust of an ugly old warlock from a nearby crate onto the cupboard and adds a dusty wig and tarnished tiara to its head.
entries.model_notes: Precise book placement and newly assembled retrieval marker. Tiara’s identity is not supplied here; retain appearance and placement without importing later canon.

entries.location: Dungeon office approach and acoustic isolation
entries.description: During the final match Harry descends stone steps into the dungeons and walks until crowd sounds disappear. Snape’s office remains in the dungeons although his teaching is now floors above. Leaving, Harry climbs the stone steps back towards the Great Hall and then the marble staircase to Gryffindor.
entries.model_notes: Dated route and loss of distant pitch sound; no proof of purpose-built soundproofing. Separate dungeon stone stairs from subsequent marble ascent.

entries.location: Snape dungeon office fixtures and detention files
entries.description: The dim office has slimy dead specimens suspended in coloured potions around the walls. Cobwebbed boxes of damaged, mouse-chewed or faded punishment record cards are piled on a table where Harry sits to copy them. A large clock ticks on the wall.
entries.model_notes: Specimen display, worktable, clock and temporary files. Harry’s suspicion that the clock runs slowly is unverified and should not drive an animation rule.

entries.description: The Fat Lady admits Harry on Quid agis, revealing a noisy common-room celebration. Ron carries a silver championship Cup; around fifty people witness Harry and Ginny’s kiss.
entries.model_notes: Dated password, trophy and crowd occupancy; not a room-capacity figure or permanent trophy display.

entries.description: Hermione reports a whole collection of old Daily Prophets in the library, from which she obtains Eileen Prince’s school photograph and news item.
entries.model_notes: Archival collection, not evidence of where within the library it is shelved; proposed Potions-award search is not confirmation of a physical display.

entries.location: Room of Requirement corridor left/right relation
entries.description: Approaching Trelawney’s fallen position from a nearby corner, Harry sees the dancing-troll tapestry on his right and the smooth stone wall hiding the Room on his left.
entries.model_notes: View-relative sides only; no compass bearing. Corridors are quiet shortly before curfew.

entries.description: Trelawney reports entering the Room to hide personal items, hearing an apparently male celebratory whoop, calling out, then being plunged into darkness and thrown headfirst outside. Harry hears her scream and finds her on the corridor floor with sherry bottles.
entries.model_notes: Room entry, voice/darkness and ejection are her report; the scream and aftermath are witnessed. Occupant identity, darkness cause and physical ejection mechanism remain unproven in this scene.

entries.description: A large blue-and-white vase stands in a nearby niche; Trelawney puts her sherry bottles into it before accompanying Harry.
entries.model_notes: Fixed decorative vessel in wall recess with temporary concealed bottles; exact recess placement not specified.

entries.description: Dumbledore stands at the office window looking out over the grounds. The setting sun casts gold then red light into the room and appears as a ruby-red glare along the horizon.
entries.model_notes: Grounds and sunset line of sight from window. Do not assign a precise azimuth or identify which window from this alone.

entries.description: Dumbledore says he has never left Hogwarts unprotected during his absences that year and will put additional protection in place that evening.
entries.model_notes: Dated security preparation; unspecified personnel/spells here. Harry’s concern about circumvention is not proof that any particular barrier has failed.

entries.description: Dumbledore waits by the oaken front doors/top stone step, then descends the steps with Harry and follows the drive downhill to gates at its bottom. In still summer twilight the air smells of warm grass, lake water and cabin wood smoke.
entries.model_notes: Front entrance → steps → descending drive → gates sequence; environmental scent sources do not supply distances or wind bearings.

entries.description: Outside the gates they turn into the deserted lane to Hogsmeade and reach the High Street, with lit windows above shops. Passing the Three Broomsticks, they then turn into the side street with the Hog’s Head’s creaking sign. They Apparate outside without entering the pub.
entries.model_notes: School boundary and off-site departure route; Hog’s Head appears empty and quiet versus the Three Broomsticks. No street lengths or bearings stated.

entries.description: Trelawney recalls staying in a room at the Hog’s Head for her interview with Dumbledore, complains of bedbugs, and describes Snape caught outside her door after claiming to have taken the wrong stairs.
entries.model_notes: Limited village lodging/stair context for the school visit; no room floor number, exact stair configuration or modern condition established.

entries.description: The small flat rocky island in the remote sea cave is described as no larger than Dumbledore’s office.
entries.model_notes: Relative scale comparison only, with no numeric dimension. The distant cave is explicitly outside Hogwarts surroundings and its underground lake is not the Hogwarts lake; do not transplant its layout, boat or Inferi into the school grounds.

entries.location: Hogsmeade High Street return and castle view
entries.description: Harry and Dumbledore Apparate into the dark High Street, lit by a few streetlamps and upper windows. Rosmerta says she saw them from her bedroom curtains. From the street the green Dark Mark is visible above Hogwarts.
entries.model_notes: Ground-level village → school-sky visibility and bedroom → High Street reported view; imagined Inferi around shops at P0002 are not real village occupants.

entries.description: Rosmerta says she keeps two brooms behind the bar; Harry Summons them, bursting open the pub’s front door as they fly into the street.
entries.model_notes: Ancillary return transport storage and bar-to-street path; not an ordinary unattended flight route through walls.

entries.location: Broom flight from village to Astronomy Tower
entries.description: They fly from the village over the dark twisting lane, cross the boundary wall into the grounds, then land over crenellated ramparts on the Astronomy Tower, the highest tower of the castle.
entries.model_notes: Aerial approach and height hierarchy. The lane is seen from above; no exact flight length or wall height.

entries.description: As Dumbledore mutters a strange language, Harry’s broom shudders crossing the boundary wall; Harry interprets this as Dumbledore undoing his own protective enchantments to admit them quickly.
entries.model_notes: Sound and shudder are observed, while barrier purpose and deliberate suspension are Harry’s interpretation. No evidence of a physically moving wall or blanket permanent removal.

entries.location: Astronomy Tower ramparts and stair door
entries.description: The tower top has crenellated ramparts/battlements and a wall against which Harry and Dumbledore can lean. A door with an iron ring opens to a spiral stair down into the castle. Initially it is closed and the ramparts are deserted.
entries.model_notes: Tower-top enclosure and descent route, not a roofed interior room. Door material is not specified by its iron handle.

entries.description: The luminous green skull and serpent-tongue Dark Mark hangs directly above the Astronomy Tower, casting dim green light over its occupants and ramparts. Draco says it was placed there to draw Dumbledore to an apparent murder scene.
entries.model_notes: Placement/light are observed; trap purpose is Draco’s account. A Mark alone is not proof that someone died at that spot before arrival.

entries.description: Draco says he spent the year repairing the broken Hogwarts Vanishing Cabinet in which Montague was trapped. Its mate is in Borgin and Burkes; together they form a passage. Montague reportedly heard both school and shop while trapped between them and eventually Apparated out at great risk. Death Eaters used the repaired pair to enter the school.
entries.model_notes: Magical off-site bypass, not a physical tunnel under the perimeter. Chapter 24 locates the Hogwarts cabinet in the hiding room. Chapter 6’s shop cabinet description can be reconciled as the off-site endpoint but its identity is not visually demonstrated by this account.

entries.location: Guard fight and tower staircase barrier
entries.description: Muffled cries from the castle below grow into fighting sounds on the spiral staircase. Four Death Eaters reach the ramparts; a voice below says the stairs are blocked and casts Reducto. Snape subsequently comes through the stair door.
entries.model_notes: Battle route and temporary stair obstruction, with barrier inferred by Harry from sounds here; exact construction clarified only by later witnesses. Snape’s passage does not prove everyone can pass.

entries.description: Snape’s curse throws Dumbledore upward and backwards over the battlements, where he disappears below the edge.
entries.model_notes: Confirms an exposed fall over the parapet to the exterior below; no measured tower height, fall duration or impact position supplied until following scene.

entries.description: Dumbledore says school communications were monitored. Draco explains that enchanted paired coins allowed messages to Rosmerta, who saw Dumbledore leave; this informed the timing of the attack.
entries.model_notes: Security limitation with remote magical communication, not a geometry feature; retain as an access/guard-state constraint. Dumbledore’s reconstruction of the bathroom delivery is a deduction, not his eyewitness account.

entries.description: From the rampart door Harry runs down the dark spiral stair, jumps its final ten steps and lands in a dim corridor. Snape escapes around a corner at the corridor’s far end.
entries.model_notes: Top-to-corridor connection; ten is the number of steps jumped, not the staircase’s total step count.

entries.description: Dust fills the corridor and roughly half its ceiling appears collapsed. Curses ricochet off stone walls, crack stone, shatter a nearby window and blast wall fragments overhead. Blood and fallen people make the floor slippery and obstructed.
entries.model_notes: Observed local damage; “half” is an impression, not surveyed area. Avoid labelling fallen people dead before later confirmation.

entries.location: Marble-stair landing portrait and destroyed armour
entries.description: After further corridor corners Harry shelters behind a suit of armour that explodes under a curse. On the landing a portrait of several wig-wearing witches is struck; its occupants flee into neighbouring paintings as the Carrows descend the marble stairs.
entries.model_notes: Armour, landing artwork cluster and dated destruction; portrait subjects move between frames, rather than physically into the corridor.

entries.location: Concealed stair shortcut with vanishing step
entries.description: Harry uses a concealed staircase shortcut, jumping a vanishing step halfway down. A tapestry at its bottom opens into a corridor occupied by Hufflepuffs; he then reaches a landing and descends the remaining marble stairs to the Entrance Hall, overtaking the Carrows.
entries.model_notes: Shortcut joins levels of the marble-stair route and contains a specific step hazard. Hufflepuff presence does not establish this corridor as their common-room entrance or basement.

entries.location: Entrance Hall blast damage and Gryffindor hourglass
entries.description: The oak front doors have been blasted open, blood smears the flagstone floor, and students shelter against the walls. The giant Gryffindor hourglass is cursed and its rubies fall rattling onto the flagstones.
entries.model_notes: Fixed score hourglass material/contents and damaged state. No dimensions, exact hourglass wall position or conditions of the other houses’ counters supplied.

entries.location: Lawn escape route and Apparition boundary
entries.description: From the front doors the fugitives cross the lawn towards the gates, intending to Disapparate beyond the school boundary. Hagrid intercepts them after emerging from his cabin; Snape eventually Disapparates just outside the boundary while Buckbeak circles the gates.
entries.model_notes: Boundary crossing is the operative restriction; gates are the route used here, not proof that Apparition is restricted to a single point outside them. Twenty yards at P0030 is a transient duel separation, not fixed site scale.

entries.description: Incendio ignites Hagrid’s wooden house, throwing orange light across the grounds and the nearby fight. Fang is trapped inside until Hagrid carries him out. Harry and Hagrid extinguish the flames with water jets, leaving a smoking wreck smelling of burnt wood and dog hair.
entries.model_notes: Dated major cabin damage, not demonstrated total destruction or reconstruction. Hagrid believes injured Bowtruckles inside have burned; their fate is not inspected. No proof all previous fixtures survive.

entries.location: Castle-front night lighting and Astronomy Tower foot
entries.description: Many castle windows are now lit; light from the open oak doors falls onto the drive and lawn, and people descend the front steps. A crowd gathers on the grass at the foot of the Astronomy Tower near the castle front, directly beneath the Dark Mark, around Dumbledore’s body. Lit wands illuminate the scene.
entries.model_notes: Tower base–front lawn relationship and temporary light sources. Harry’s distant imagined body at P0083 is superseded by close observation; no exact tower-to-door spacing.

entries.location: Front lawn–hospital route and ward bed positions
entries.description: Ginny leads Harry up the front steps, across the ruby-strewn Entrance Hall towards the marble staircase, then to the hospital wing. Neville lies in a bed near the ward doors and Bill in another near the far end, with chairs around it.
entries.model_notes: Ward longitudinal relationship from entrance to far bed; no exact bed count or absolute floor. Pomfrey conjures an extra chair, so visitor furniture can change.

entries.description: Fawkes sings outside in the darkness; his lament echoes across the grounds and through castle windows and remains audible in the hospital wing and deserted corridors.
entries.model_notes: Magical mourning soundscape; subjective emotional effect is not a measured acoustic property or evidence of a precise outdoor perch.

entries.description: McGonagall reports corridor patrols, guards covering every secret passage out of school, powerful enchantments on every castle entrance and an expectation that nobody could fly in.
entries.model_notes: Defenders’ report of intended security state, not an omniscient guarantee; Cabinet bypass defeated it. Earlier aerial entry required Dumbledore’s intervention.

entries.description: Ron and Ginny report Draco emerging with a Hand of Glory, which illuminates only its holder. He throws Darkness Powder into the corridor; neither Lumos nor Incendio penetrates it, and guards must feel their way to a lit corridor while people run past.
entries.model_notes: Temporary visually opaque zone and selective light source. Exact cloud extent and persistence unspecified; companions’ identities and guiding method are partly their reconstruction.

entries.location: Astronomy stair cursed barrier and collapse
entries.description: Tonks reports a curse blocking the stair behind the Death Eaters; Neville is thrown upward trying to enter. Lupin sees Snape pass through and is himself repelled. A later hex drops half the corridor ceiling and breaks the stair-blocking curse.
entries.model_notes: Selectively passable barrier and explicit destruction sequence. Dark-Mark eligibility is Harry’s guess at P0080, not established; do not implement that as confirmed authentication.

entries.description: Hermione and Luna wait outside the dungeon office. Flitwick runs down from the fighting and enters it; Snape emerges, tells them to attend to Flitwick, and they find him unconscious on the office floor.
entries.model_notes: Observed by reporting witnesses. Snape stunning Flitwick is their inference; Harry’s imagined marble-stair ascent at P0073 is not a witnessed route.

entries.description: The circular office remains much as before: silver instruments whir and smoke on spindle-legged tables, the sword in its case gleams in moonlight, and the Sorting Hat is on a shelf behind the desk. Fawkes’s perch is empty. A new sleeping portrait of Dumbledore in a golden frame hangs over the desk.
entries.model_notes: Office is now used by McGonagall; no black drapery or body is actually present—those are Harry’s expectations, explicitly contradicted by observation.

entries.location: Everard portrait high on office wall
entries.description: A sallow-faced wizard with a short black fringe returns to his canvas high on the wall and speaks; McGonagall addresses him as Everard.
entries.model_notes: Portrait identity, appearance and height relationship; no precise frame dimensions. His Minister-arrival news does not show an actual physical route from the Ministry.

entries.description: From the office window McGonagall looks down over the grounds to watch for the Minister and later sees him arriving with a delegation.
entries.model_notes: Confirmed downward exterior approach view; exact gates/path visible and viewing bearing unspecified.

entries.description: On the return to Gryffindor, the Fat Lady admits Harry without waiting for a password. The crowded common room connects across to the boys’ dormitory door; Ron waits on his bed and Harry sits on his own four-poster.
entries.model_notes: Discretionary access exception and repeated room-to-dorm relationship; no new room dimensions.

entries.description: The grounds fall silent when Fawkes stops singing, and Harry understands that the phoenix has left Hogwarts for good.
entries.model_notes: Cessation is observed; permanent departure is Harry’s unverified conviction here, not a followed flight. Empty office perch is independently seen at P0125.
